# `aitbc resource allocate`

Allocate CPU, memory, GPU, and storage resources for an agent.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc resource allocate [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--agent-id` | text | — | yes | Agent ID to allocate resources for |
| `--cpu-cores` | float | — | no | Requested CPU cores |
| `--memory-gb` | float | — | no | Requested memory (GB) |
| `--gpu-count` | float | — | no | Requested GPU count |
| `--gpu-memory-gb` | float | — | no | Requested GPU memory (GB) |
| `--storage-gb` | float | — | no | Requested storage (GB) |
| `--network-bandwidth` | float | — | no | Requested network bandwidth (Mbps) |
| `--optimization-target` | choice | `efficiency` | no | Optimization target for allocation |
| `--priority` | choice | `normal` | no | Priority level |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc resource allocate --agent-id <agent_id>
```
